Dhaka today is not merely a waterlogged city.
It is a metropolis built over the graves of its floodplains—a city that once coexisted with rivers and seasonal wetlands, but has steadily replaced them with concrete.
And the price of that transformation is now being paid by millions of residents with every monsoon, every flooded street and every neighborhood that disappears under water after a few hours of rain.

item.title: Formal charges in Shapla Chattar case to be filed on Monday
item.description:
The prosecution will submit formal charges to the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) on Monday in the crimes against humanity case over the alleged killings during the 2013 Shapla Chattar operation, Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam said on Saturday.
Speaking at a discussion titled "Human Rights Violations and Access to Justice for Victims" at the CIRDAP auditorium in Dhaka, Aminul Islam said the ICT's investigation agency had completed its probe into the events of May 5, 2013, and submitted its report to the Chief Prosecutor's Office.
After reviewing the findings, prosecutors prepared the formal charge sheet, which will be placed before the tribunal on Monday, marking the next stage in the judicial process, he said.
According to the prosecution, more than 40 people, including former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, have been named as accused in the case. The full list of defendants will be disclosed when the formal charges are filed.
Nine people are currently in custody in connection with the case. They include former minister Dr Dipu Moni, former state minister for home affairs Shamsul Haque Tuku, retired Major General Ziaul Ahsan, former inspector general of police AKM Shahidul Hoque, former deputy inspector general Mollah Nazrul Islam, Shahriar Kabir, president of the advisory committee of the Ghatak Dalal Nirmul Committee, former DIG Abdul Jalil Mondal, and journalists Farzana Rupa and Mozammel Babu.
Prosecution sources said the investigation report names 41 accused, including Sheikh Hasina, former army chief General Aziz Ahmed, journalists Mozammel Babu and Farzana Rupa, and writer Shahriar Kabir. Detailed information is expected to be disclosed at a formal press briefing.
On May 5, 2013, Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh staged a rally at Shapla Chattar in Dhaka's Motijheel, demanding implementation of its 13-point charter.
Following a day of tensions and clashes, members of the police, Rapid Action Battalion (RAB), and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) carried out a joint overnight operation to clear the area. Allegations that numerous people were killed during the operation later prompted an investigation by the International Crimes Tribunal into possible crimes against humanity.

item.title: India’s education minister resigns, end called to Delhi protests
item.description:
India’s Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday after mass youth-led protests demanded his ouster in anger over a string of irregularities in potentially life-changing exams.
Thousands of young people gathered in the capital and in other parts of the country this week, under the banner of the social media-driven Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), demanding an overhaul of the education system and Pradhan’s resignation.
“I am pained to see the events of the past 10 days. This is not a matter of personal prestige for me,” Pradhan said in a statement posted on social media platform X.
“I have sent my resignation letter to the prime minister,” Pradhan said in his letter in Hindi.
The CJP said after Pradhan’s resignation that all their demands had been met in another round of talks and that they were calling off the protests that were centered on the Jantar Mantar demonstration site in central New Delhi.
Police had fired tear gas and charged with batons at protesters as they tried to march from the site to parliament this week.
The government held two rounds of talks with CJP leaders on Monday and Friday but little headway was made initially, with the youth-led movement sticking to their demands.
Pradhan announced his resignation before the third round of talks.
“India’s youth power is the real strength of this nation. My resolve is that we will not let the country’s youth get trapped in a vicious cycle of confusion,” he said.
Protesters erupted in joy after Pradhan’s announcement.
“We have done it,” CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said to a thunderous response by hundreds of protesters.
The movement has evolved to include concerns over unemployment, opportunities for young people and what critics brand as Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s increasingly authoritarian style of governance.
The protests became one of the biggest challenges to Hindu nationalist Modi’s administration since his 2024 re-election.
The protesters’ other demands included compensation for those affected by examination irregularities and for legal cases against protesters to be dropped, according to CJP spokesman Ashutosh Ranka.
India’s opposition leader Rahul Gandhi threw his weight behind protesters in support of their cause, calling Pradhan’s resignation a “huge step.”
Gandhi called for Modi to “apologize” and respect students and India’s future generations.
“Action should be taken against those guilty of violence against students,” he said.
Sunil, 27, who came to the protest site for the first time on Saturday to “experience the atmosphere,” said it was “truly electrifying, especially after the minister’s resignation.”
“What the young people did was commendable,” he told AFP.

item.title: Bangladesh among contenders as Brazil plan friendly in India during October FIFA window
item.description:
Bangladesh has emerged as one of the countries in contention to host Brazil for an international friendly, although India has moved into pole position to welcome the five-time FIFA World Cup champions during the October FIFA international window, according to reports from Brazil.
ESPN Brasil reported that the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) is in advanced negotiations with Indian organizers and stakeholders over a proposed friendly in Kolkata, with discussions having begun during the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico.
The report added that, besides India, Bangladesh, Singapore and Qatar have also made firm approaches to host the Selecao as Brazil look to finalize a third friendly during the September-October international window.
Brazil are scheduled to play two confirmed friendlies in Australia, facing opponents in Townsville on September 25 and Brisbane on September 29. The CBF is now working to secure a third fixture, with India emerging as the leading candidate.
According to the report, Brazil's interest in playing in the Indian subcontinent has been driven by the overwhelming support the team received from Indian fans throughout the 2026 World Cup. The Selecao enjoyed widespread backing on social media during the tournament despite their campaign ending in disappointment.
Managed by Carlo Ancelotti, Brazil entered the World Cup as one of the favorites but were eliminated by Norway in the Round of 16, ending their bid for a record-extending sixth world title.
Should the Kolkata fixture be finalized, Indian fans would get the chance to watch some of Brazil's biggest stars, including Vinicius Jr, Bruno Guimarães, Matheus Cunha and Gabriel Magalhães.
A Brazil appearance in India would also revive memories of one of the country's most iconic football moments. In 1977, Brazilian legend Pelé visited Kolkata with New York Cosmos for a famous exhibition match against Mohun Bagan, attracting a packed crowd and cementing the city's reputation as one of South Asia's football capitals.
While Bangladesh remains among the countries hoping to bring the Selecao to their shores, the report suggests India is currently the frontrunner to host Brazil's final friendly of the October FIFA window. No official confirmation has yet been made by the CBF or the All India Football Federation.

item.title: Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha heading to Chile after stellar World Cup campaign
item.description:
Vozinha, the 40-year-old goalkeeper who was one of the heroes of Cape Verde's fairytale run at the World Cup, is signing for Colo Colo, the Chilean club announced.
"Vozinha is set to become a Colo Colo player; he will arrive in Chile in the coming days, undergo the necessary medical tests and will then be presented here at the Monumental Stadium," club president Anibal Mosa told reporters ahead of a league match on Friday evening.
Vozinha starred at the World Cup with heroic displays in a 0-0 group-stage draw against eventual champions Spain and in a 3-2 extra-time loss to finalists Argentina in the knock-out rounds.
The goalie, whose full name is Josimar Jose Evora Dias, will move to Chile from Chaves of the Portuguese second division. Although he did not sign his first professional contract until he was 26, he has also played in Cyprus, Slovakia, Moldova and Angola.
"He's in very good form; that's why we're signing him," said Mosa.
Vozinha has also become a social media star, with help from Brazilian influencer Casimiro. The goalkeeper's Instagram following has soared from 50,000 to nearly 30 million.
Colo Colo, 34-time Chilean champions, hold a comfortable lead in the table midway through the current season.

item.title: 6 more die with measles symptoms, death toll rises to 816
item.description:
Six more people died with measles symptoms across the country in the 24 hours until 8:00 am today, Saturday, all of them residents of Dhaka district.

According to official figures, a total of 721 people have died with measles symptoms since 15 March. In addition, 95 deaths have been confirmed as measles through laboratory testing. Altogether, the number of deaths linked to confirmed measles and measles symptoms has risen to 816.

US measles cases hit 31-year high to 2,318 as vaccinations decline

The information was disclosed in the Directorate General of Health Services' (DGHS) regular measles bulletin published today, Saturday.

The DGHS statistics do not provide an age-wise breakdown. Epidemiologists say measles can affect people of all ages, although children are the most vulnerable. During an outbreak, all deaths involving measles symptoms are treated as measles-related deaths.

According to the DGHS report, 613 more people developed measles symptoms across the country over the past 24 hours. Since 15 March, the total number of people with measles symptoms has reached 122,763.

Bangladesh emerges as world’s worst-hit by measles over past 6 months

Meanwhile, laboratory tests confirmed 78 new measles cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed infections since 15 March to 15,272.

Hospital admission data show that 105,298 patients with measles symptoms have been admitted to hospitals since 15 March. Of them, 101,535 have recovered and been discharged.

According to the World Health Organization (WHO), Bangladesh recorded 42,174 cases of measles or measles symptoms during the six months from December last year to May this year, the highest number reported by any country during that period.

item.title: Samsung launches new foldable smartphones
item.description:
SKOREA-TELECOMMUNICATION-SAMSUNG

South Korean technology giant Samsung unveiled new, sleeker smartphone models Wednesday priced more than previous models as artificial intelligence raises component costs.

One of the models resembles a miniature tablet when unfolded.

Samsung, which launched the high-end products in London, aims to reaffirm its dominance in the foldable smartphone market, where it has operated since 2019, ahead of a potential move by US rival Apple this year.

"By setting a new standard for foldables, we are once again advancing the premium mobile experience," said TM Roh, head of Samsung''s mobile division.

The most innovative device unveiled Wednesday is the Galaxy Z Fold8. Measuring 4.5 millimetres thick when unfolded, it features a 7.6-inch, 4:3 aspect ratio screen optimised for video viewing.

Its starting price is set at USD 1,900.

"Galaxy Z Fold8 is the clear star of the show," said Paolo Pescatore, a technology analyst for PP Foresight.

"It underscores Samsung's dominance of the foldable category and its determination to expand the market with a device for almost every type of user."

"Attention now turns to Apple's September event and whether it will finally unveil its long-anticipated move into foldables.

Samsung's new top-of-the-range model is the Z Fold8 Ultra -- successor to the Z Fold7 -- whose retail price starts at USD 2,100. It measures just 4.1 millimetres in thickness and weighs 215 grammes.

The Z Flip8 -- a pocket-sized model geared more toward social media use -- is the cheapest new model, with a starting price of USD 1,200.

The higher prices are caused by soaring costs of memory chips, which are in growing demand owing to their strategic role in powering artificial intelligence.

Apple last month cited this reason when raising the prices of its Macs and iPads.

"Apple is about to do for foldables what it has done for every category it has entered, which is legitimise it for the mainstream," said Francisco Jeronimo at telecommunications analyst group IDC.

"Samsung has to defend the category it created, and that's why it cannot 1play it safe," he added.

item.title: Faridpur farmers expect bumper jute harvest, seek fair prices
item.description:
Farmers in Faridpur are busy harvesting and retting jute cultivated on 87,000 hectares this season, with favourable weather boosting hopes of bumper yield. However, growers remain concerned over rising production costs and uncertainty surrounding market prices.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), nearly 90% of farmers in the district cultivated jute this season. The production target has been set at 195,000 metric tonnes, with an expected average yield of 2.24 metric tonnes per hectare.
DAE Deputy Director Shahaduzzaman said favourable weather conditions throughout the growing season have increased the likelihood of achieving the production target.
"We are optimistic about meeting this season's target as weather conditions have remained favourable for jute cultivation," he said.
He added that Faridpur contributes around 30% of the country's total jute production, with the district's fibre widely recognised for its quality.
Despite the positive production outlook, farmers say higher input costs have squeezed their profit margins. Limited rainfall at the beginning of the season forced many to irrigate their fields, while rising prices of fertilisers, fuel and other agricultural inputs increased cultivation expenses. Labour costs have also continued to climb.
Farmers in Saltha, including Hasem Matubbar, Harun Molla and Saiful Islam, said they are currently harvesting and retting their crop but fear incurring losses if they do not receive fair prices at the end of the season.
They urged the government to procure jute at the announced price on time and improve market management to ensure fair returns, saying such measures would encourage farmers to expand jute cultivation.
Faridpur Farmers' Association President Manik Majumdar said strong production alone would not guarantee farmers' livelihoods.
"Ensuring fair prices, improving market access and reducing production costs are essential to making jute cultivation profitable," he said. "That will help preserve Faridpur's position as one of Bangladesh's leading jute-producing districts."

item.title: Heavy rains push up vegetable, fish prices in Gopalganj
item.description:
Prices of vegetables in Gopalganj have doubled or even tripled over the past 10 days following heavy rainfall that damaged crops and disrupted supplies, leaving low and middle-income families struggling to cope with soaring food costs.
A visit to Boro Bazar in the town showed that no vegetable was selling for less than Tk 60 per kilogram. Okra, previously priced at Tk 20-25 per kg, is now selling for Tk 60. Sweet pumpkin price has increased from Tk 25-30 to Tk 60, while pointed gourd, ridge gourd and teasel gourd are selling at Tk 80 per kg after rising sharply from Tk 30-35. Sponge gourd now costs Tk 60, and both bitter gourd and taro corms have reached Tk 80 per kg.
A medium-sized bottle gourd that recently sold for Tk 30-40 now costs Tk 80-100. Papaya remains the cheapest vegetable at Tk 40 per kg, while green chilies have jumped to Tk 200 per kg from Tk 80 just 10 days ago.
Fish prices have also climbed significantly. Hilsa weighing one kilogram is selling for nearly Tk 3,000, while smaller hilsa weighing 350-400 grams costs around Tk 1,500. Farmed varieties, including pangas, rohit, catla and silver carp, have become Tk 25-50 more expensive per kilogram. Rohit now sells for Tk 500-600 per kg, up from Tk 450-480 only a few days ago.
Fish trader Johor blamed the increase on heavy rains in fish-producing areas, saying floodwaters caused farmed fish to escape from ponds, reducing market supply. Although hilsa prices briefly declined last week due to increased seasonal catches, they have since risen again, pushing overall fish prices higher.
Consumers say the rising costs are placing severe pressure on household budgets. Shopper Saidul Islam Shovon said many families can no longer afford to buy all the essentials. Another customer, Md. Ehsanul Alam, said his family has reduced fish consumption because prices continue to rise while incomes remain unchanged.
Vegetable traders said continuous rainfall has damaged crops and sharply reduced supplies reaching wholesale markets. They noted that vegetable prices usually increase during the monsoon season, but this year's prolonged rainfall has made the situation far worse.
Dr. Md. Mamunur Rahman, Deputy Director of the Department of Agricultural Extension in Gopalganj, said above-normal rainfall in July inundated 85 hectares of vegetable fields, damaging crops including bitter gourd, bottle gourd, pumpkin, papaya, pointed gourd, okra, chili and yardlong beans. The losses have affected 1,360 vegetable farmers and significantly reduced local market supplies.
District Agricultural Marketing Officer Arif Hossain said authorities are continuing regular market monitoring and have advised traders to avoid excessive profit-taking while maintaining reasonable margins between wholesale and retail prices.
He added that with local production declining, most vegetables are now being brought into Gopalganj from other districts, contributing to higher prices.

item.title: Pipe bomb planted to target Rath Yatra
item.description:
The Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit said the pipe bomb had been planted to target the Ulto Rath Yatra procession after police recovered the powerful improvised explosive device (IED) beneath Motijheel Metro Rail Station in Dhaka on Friday.
Sub-Inspector (SI) Mirza Mohammad Mukta of Motijheel Police Station subsequently filed a case under the Explosives Act against unidentified individuals
According to the case, police received information about a suspicious bomb-like object along the procession route and recovered an umbrella containing a powerful pipe bomb before the religious procession reached the area. Authorities said the device was detected in time, preventing a potentially serious incident.
A passerby was injured during the controlled disposal of the bomb on Friday night. The injured, 66-year-old Miraj Ahmed, an employee of the Ministry of Education, sustained splinter injuries to his left eye. After receiving primary treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital, he was referred to the National Institute of Ophthalmology in Agargaon for further treatment.
According to the case documents, SI Mirza Mohammad Mukta was on duty with the "Honda Mobile" patrol unit to provide security for the Ulto Rath Yatra procession.
The procession began at Dhakeshwari National Temple, passed through Shapla Chattar in Motijheel and was scheduled to conclude at Swamibagh Ashram.
During the evening, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Control Room received information from the Traffic Division about a suspicious bomb-like object near the procession route. The device had been concealed inside an umbrella, and witnesses reported seeing a blinking light on it.
Following instructions from senior officials, SI Mukta and other officers reached the area beside the generator room of Motijheel Metro Rail Station at around 6:20pm and secured the location where the device had been found.
Police then requested participants in the procession to avoid the area, telling them there had been an electrical short circuit, allowing the procession to continue safely toward Swamibagh Ashram.
After the procession had passed through the area, members of the DMP Bomb Disposal Unit carried out a controlled explosion and safely neutralized the device, according to the case.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune on Saturday evening, Additional Commissioner of Dhaka Metropolitan Police and chief of the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit Mohammad Shamsul Haque said: "The powerful pipe bomb had been planted to target the Rath Yatra procession."
He said the explosive had been attached to an umbrella in a way that opening it would have triggered the blast, potentially causing multiple casualties.
Describing the device, he said: "It was an improvised explosive device (IED) in the form of a pipe bomb. It contained sulfur, a large quantity of sharp metal fragments and barbed wire. The device was connected to a battery and an electrical circuit and was designed so that pressing the release button to open the umbrella would detonate the bomb."
Shamsul Haque confirmed that one passerby was injured during the bomb disposal operation and said the casualties could have been much higher had the area been crowded.
He added that investigators have yet to identify those responsible or determine their motive. He urged the public not to panic, saying law enforcement agencies and other relevant authorities are investigating the incident to identify and apprehend those involved.

item.title: 439 fresh cases of dengue infection reported, 1 death overnight
item.description:
Health officials on Saturday said they recorded 439 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts killing at least one person in the past 24 hours.
"During the period, (of the 439) 83 patients were hospitalized in Barisal division while 75 in Chittagong division, 77 in Dhaka division, 46 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and 41 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) areas, 41 in Khulna division, 19 in Mymensingh division, 26 in Rajshahi division, 30 in Rangpur division and one Sylhet division, a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) statement said.
Since the start of the dengue onslaughts Bangladesh this year witnessed, so far, 40 deaths while the disease inflicted 12,640.
The dengue last year claimed 413 lives and inflicted 1,02,861 people in the country.
Besides, the mosquito-borne disease claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in 2024.

item.title: Registration begins for students who missed July 13 HSC exams
item.description:
Students who were unable to sit for the July 13, 2026 Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations due to adverse weather conditions will be allowed to take a retest, the Inter-Education Board Examination Controllers' Committee announced.
An urgent notice issued on Saturday, signed by Prof Jesmin Taslima Banu, examination controller of the Dhaka Education Board and convener of the Inter-Education Board Examination Controllers' Committee, instructed eligible students to register for the retest at their respective examination centres by July 29.
According to the notice, the opportunity applies to HSC and equivalent candidates under all education boards except the Chittagong Education Board who missed the Physics first paper, Accounting first aaper, or Logic first paper examinations held on July 13 because of inclement weather.
The provision also covers students under the Bangladesh Madrasa Education Board who missed the English second paper examination and those under the Bangladesh Technical Education Board who were absent from the Office Management examination for the same reason.
Examination centres have been instructed to submit the list of registered candidates to the respective education boards' examination controllers on an urgent basis by July 30.

item.title: Three years on, Dhaka still waits for flood defence plan
item.description:
Nearly three years after approving an ambitious climate resilience blueprint to reduce flooding and restore wetlands, Rajuk has made little visible progress in implementing one of its flagship proposals -- a network of 14 eco-parks and 55 water parks -- leaving Dhaka increasingly exposed to monsoon flooding and rising temperatures.
The lack of implementation has come under renewed scrutiny after recent heavy rainfall submerged large parts of the capital, disrupting transport and daily life and raising questions over why one of the city’s most significant long-term flood mitigation plans remains largely on paper.
Approved under the Detailed Area Plan (DAP) 2022-2035, the proposal envisioned a network of eco-parks and water parks across Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj to preserve wetlands, restore natural drainage, retain stormwater and strengthen the capital’s resilience against climate change.
Heavy rainfall inundates parts of the capital, disrupting traffic movement and normal daily life. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
The plan identified these conservation areas as critical natural infrastructure capable of reducing waterlogging, recharging groundwater, moderating urban temperatures, protecting biodiversity and preventing further encroachment on remaining wetlands.
Among the proposed projects are the largest eco-park centred on Bhawal National Park in Gazipur and a 587-acre water park in the Goran-Chatbari area.
Additional conservation sites were planned in Uttarkhan, Nasirabad, Keraniganj, Rupganj and Narayanganj.
Urban planners say the projects are intended to reverse decades of wetland destruction that have severely weakened Dhaka’s natural drainage system.
Dr Adil Mohammed Khan, executive director of the Institute for Planning and Development (IPD), said repeated failures to implement urban planning recommendations have contributed directly to the city’s worsening environmental crisis.
Heavy rainfall inundates parts of the capital, disrupting traffic movement and normal daily life. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
“Dhaka now goes under water after even a short spell of rain. Heat has become unbearable, while groundwater is declining. These are the cumulative consequences of ignoring planning decisions,” he said.
He warned that unless the proposed conservation areas are protected and developed soon, many could eventually be lost to residential and commercial expansion.
The recommendations are not new.
The Dhaka Metropolitan Development Plan (1995-2015) identified five permanent retention ponds as essential flood-control infrastructure, while the 2010 Detailed Area Plan proposed preserving major retention areas in Kallyanpur, Goran-Chatbari, Nasirabad, Beraid and Uttarkhan.
Many of those areas have since been partially encroached upon or filled despite remaining designated as retention zones in both the current DAP and Dhaka Wasa’s Drainage Master Plan.
Planning experts say the latest DAP goes beyond conventional retention ponds by allowing wetlands to function as natural flood buffers while preserving their ecological role.
Rajuk Chief Town Planner Md Ashraful Islam acknowledged that implementation has yet to become visible despite the importance of the projects.
“There is no alternative to developing these eco-parks and water parks if Dhaka is to become more livable,” he said.
He said Rajuk has initiated work on a park in Motijheel and taken a policy decision to develop another in Ghatarchar, but admitted that the broader program requires coordinated action involving Rajuk, the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, Dhaka North and South city corporations, Dhaka Wasa, the Department of Environment, the Bangladesh Water Development Board and the Ministry of Land.
Urban planners warn that as climate change brings more intense rainfall and rapid urbanization continues to replace wetlands with concrete, every year of delay leaves Dhaka more vulnerable to flooding, extreme heat and environmental degradation.
For them, the question is no longer whether the capital needs its planned eco-parks and water parks, but why one of Bangladesh’s most important climate adaptation strategies remains largely unimplemented three years after its approval.

item.title: Health minister finds expired medicines at Morrelganj health complex
item.description:
hHealth and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Hossain made a surprise visit to Morrelganj Upazila Health Complex in Bagerhat on Saturday and found a large stock of expired medicines worth lakhs of taka in the facility's abandoned building.
During the inspection, the minister also reviewed the quality of healthcare services, food provided to patients, cleanliness and the shortage of doctors at the health complex.
After visiting different departments, he expressed dissatisfaction over the irregularities and other shortcomings.
"The poor people of my country do not get medicines, while expired medicines worth lakhs of taka are lying in the store," the minister said.
He directed the authorities concerned to take immediate steps to address the problems identified during the visit. The minister also inspected a nearby private clinic in the area.
Speaking to reporters afterwards, Sakhawat Hossain said the country's healthcare system had deteriorated due to irregularities, corruption and money laundering during the previous government.
He said the current government is working to restore the health sector and expressed hope that people in the area would receive better healthcare services in the future.
"We want our poor and hardworking people to receive services with the facilities we have. We are planning to upgrade the hospital from 50 beds to 100 beds. The tender process will begin soon and work will start afterwards," he said.
The minister said he had taken note of all the issues identified during the inspection and would discuss them with the higher authorities in Dhaka to ensure necessary action is taken in the public interest.
Later, he visited nearby Sarankhola Upazila Health Complex for a similar inspection.
Finally, the minister visited Bagerhat Sadar Hospital.
Bagerhat Deputy Commissioner Golam Md Baten and Superintendent of Police Hasan Mohammad Nasher Rikabdar, among others, accompanied the minister during the visit.

item.title: Maldives' president warmly welcomes Dr Khalilur as special guest of Independence Day celebrations
item.description:
Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu on Saturday evening warmly welcomed Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman and expressed his sincere appreciation for the minister's visit to the Maldives as the "special guest" of the government at the 61st Independence Day celebrations.
The foreign minister, who is visiting the Maldives from Saturday to Monday, paid a courtesy call on President Muizzu at the President's Office.
During the call, discussions focused on ways to further strengthen bilateral relations, with particular emphasis on multilateral cooperation, educational opportunities, and people-to-people exchanges.
Both sides highlighted the longstanding bilateral relations and enduring friendship between the two countries.
They reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation across areas of mutual interest for the mutual benefit of both countries.
President Muizzu also hosted an evening tea in honour of Dr Khalilur.
The Maldives is celebrating its 61st Independence Day on July 26, commemorating the end of British rule in 1965.
High-profile international delegates, including Saudi Royal Prince Dr Mansour bin Mutaib bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, as the "guest of honour," arrived in the Maldives to join the national celebrations.
Dr Khalilur arrived in the Maldives via Doha from Manila, the Philippines, a senior official told UNB.
This is the first official visit to the Maldives by Dr Khalilur since assuming office as the minister of Foreign Affairs of Bangladesh on February 17, 2026.
His visit is seen as a "significant milestone" in further strengthening the longstanding and cordial relations between Bangladesh and the Maldives.
"The visit sets the stage for enhanced cooperation in the years ahead," said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives.
Dr Khalilur was received by the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Iruthisham Adam, and senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
During the visit, Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur is scheduled to meet with Foreign Minister Iruthisham Adam.
The discussions will focus on further strengthening the longstanding partnership between the Maldives and Bangladesh, reviewing the broad spectrum of bilateral cooperation, and exploring new opportunities to expand collaboration in areas of mutual interest.
The two ministers will also exchange views on regional and international developments and reaffirm their commitment to continued cooperation in regional and multilateral fora.

item.title: Fakhrul: Party forum to make final decision on next president
item.description:
LGRD and Cooperatives Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Saturday said that his party has not yet decided whether its nominee for the country's next president will come from within BNP or be a consensus candidate from outside the party.
Speaking to reporters after inaugurating the 36th Annual Planning Conference at Rural Development Academy in Bogra, he said the party's highest policymaking body would discuss the matter.
Fakhrul also said a final decision would be made following deliberations at the standing committee in accordance with the Constitution and relevant laws. Responding to speculation linking his own name to the presidency, he declined to comment, reiterating that only the party forum would make the final decision.

item.title: BB governor visits Nila Market to promote 'Bangla QR', pays via QR code
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman, visited Nila Market in Purbachal New Town on Saturday as part of an ongoing campaign to promote the "Bangla QR" digital payment system.
Senior officials from the central bank, alongside representatives from relevant commercial banks and payment service providers (PSPs), accompanied the Governor during the visit.
During his tour of various shops in the market, the Governor interacted with local traders and shoppers, highlighting the benefits of digital transactions.
He urged everyone to adopt Bangla QR as a safe, fast, and convenient payment method for daily purchases.
To demonstrate the system firsthand, Governor Rahman personally bought several items from market vendors and settled the bills using Bangla QR.
He expressed optimism that the initiative would boost enthusiasm and raise awareness among both business owners and the general public to adopt Bangla QR in their everyday transactions.

item.title: KU students continue protest as administration fails to meet demands
item.description:
Students of Khulna University (KU) continued their protest, keeping all administrative and academic buildings locked despite several measures announced by the university authorities to resolve the ongoing crisis.
As of 10am on Saturday, all administrative and academic buildings, except the guest house, remained closed. Discussions between the university administration and student representatives were underway, with authorities focusing on addressing the students’ three-point demand.
KU Registrar Professor Dr SM Mahbubur Rahman said the administration was giving serious consideration to the students’ demands but the students remained firm in their position.
“Administrative and academic buildings are still locked. Discussions are continuing, and the issue of accepting the students’ demands is being taken seriously,” he said.
The unrest began after female students of Bijoy ’24 Hall allegedly caught canteen worker Imam Hasan secretly recording videos inside a washroom using a mobile phone on the night of July 22. The incident sparked anger among students, who raised concerns over safety and demanded immediate action.
Following the incident, the university administration handed over Imam Hasan and his wife Rupa Moni to law enforcement on July 23. A case was filed against them under several sections of the Pornography Control Act, 2012. The two accused were produced before a court, where they gave confessional statements under Section 164 and were later sent to jail after their bail petitions were rejected.
The university has formed a three-member committee to investigate whether there was any negligence by the Bijoy ’24 Hall authorities. The hall administration has also formed a separate five-member committee to examine the incident.
As preventive measures, the university has banned mobile phones for canteen workers in residential halls, moved to cancel the contract of the Bijoy ’24 Hall canteen operator, and decided that female halls will have only female workers in their canteens. Experts will also inspect the hall washrooms for possible hidden cameras.
However, students rejected the steps and announced an indefinite shutdown of academic and administrative activities until their demands are met. Their demands include maximum punishment for Imam Hasan, accountability of hall authorities, permanent dismissal of two teachers accused in separate sexual harassment cases, and cancellation of the registration of the student organisation ‘Spandan 24.’
The administration said it would continue discussions and take necessary action according to university rules.

item.title: Iran Guards say stopped four ships trying to transit Hormuz strait
item.description:
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Saturday their forces stopped four ships attempting to transit the strategic Strait of Hormuz over the past 24 hours.
“Four vessels that had intended to transit through the southern area of the Strait of Hormuz via an illegal and unsafe route were stopped over the past 24 hours after warning shots were fired by the IRGC Navy,” the Guards said in a statement quoted by state television, adding that the ships had “altered course.”
Iran has in recent weeks hit tankers using a route hugging the Omani coast to traverse the strait, in a bid to strongarm vessels into using its own waters and pay for safe passage.

item.title: Nahid ruled out of Australia Tests with side strain
item.description:
Bangladesh suffered a major setback ahead of their historic Test tour of Australia as pace spearhead Nahid Rana was ruled out of the two-match series with a Grade 2 left side strain, the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) announced today.
Nahid, one of the fastest bowlers in contemporary cricket and a key figure in Bangladesh's pace attack, sustained the injury during a match on July 17 in Zimbabwe tour. Subsequent scans confirmed the severity of the strain.
According to the BCB, the right-arm pacer is expected to require around four weeks for tissue healing, followed by another two to four weeks to gradually build up his bowling workload, with his overall recovery estimated at six to eight weeks from the date of injury.
Nahid's absence comes as a significant blow to Bangladesh, who are set to play their first Test series in Australia in 23 years.
There was, however, encouraging news regarding left-arm pacer Shoriful Islam, who is recovering from a Grade 1 left hamstring injury sustained on July 14.
The BCB said Shoriful is progressing well through his rehabilitation and is expected to resume bowling on July 29 before undergoing a fitness assessment around August 12. While he is unlikely to be available for the opening Test, he is expected to be in contention for the second match, subject to successfully completing his bowling workload and receiving medical clearance.
Wicketkeeper-batter Liton Das is also targeting a return for the second Test after undergoing platelet-rich plasma (PRP) treatment in Singapore for a left calf muscle injury.
The BCB said Liton will begin a progressive running and conditioning programme on July 28 and is scheduled for a fitness assessment around August 13. If he completes his rehabilitation successfully, he is expected to be available for selection for the second Test.
Meanwhile, pacer Tanzim Hasan Sakib remains under rehabilitation, with a follow-up scan by an overseas specialist indicating that he will continue his recovery programme before undergoing another scan in eight to ten weeks. His return to play timeline will depend on fracture healing, with his availability currently expected towards the end of the year.
Left-arm pacer Mustafizur Rahman is also continuing his rehabilitation from a right hamstring and calf injury. He is expected to undergo a fitness assessment at the end of July and if his recovery progresses as planned, he should be available for selection after August 18.
The opening Test of the series will begin in Darwin on August 13, while the second and final Test is scheduled to be played in Mackay from August 22.

item.title: Kishan, Varma hit half centuries as India win Zimbabwe T20 series
item.description:
Ishan Kishan and Tilak Varma struck half centuries to overshadow teenage star Vaibhav Sooryavanshi asIndia beat Zimbabwe by 90 runs on Saturday to win a Twenty20 international series.
Wicketkeeper Kishan made 81 off 44 balls and unbeaten Varma 60 from 29 deliveries at Harare Sports Club as the tourists took an unassailable 2-0 lead. The final match is scheduled for Sunday.
A second victory in three days marked a turnaround for India who arrived in southern Africa after series losses in Ireland and England.
Sooryavanshi, the 15-year-old batting prodigy who scored his maiden T20I half century on Thursday in Harare, scored 20 runs.
Put in to bat, India posted 219-5 with whirlwind stands of Kishan and Varma tormenting the Zimbabwe bowlers. Zimbabwe were all out for 129 in reply.
Batting at No. 3, Kishan put on 66 runs for the third wicket with captain Shreyas Iyer (25) and 95 for the fourth with Varma.
Kishan struck two sixes and nine fours before slicing a Newman Nyamhuri delivery outside off stump. Brian Bennett darted forward from deep to pull off a superb catch.
Varma, like Kishan, part of the 2026 T20I World Cup-winning team, struck three sixes and five fours in his undefeated knock.
Sooryavanshi hit a six and three fours off nine balls before a sliced a pull off a Richard Ngarava delivery was caught by Blessing Muzarabani retreating from mid on.
Zimbabwe lie 10 places below India in the world T20I rankings and were always struggling with only opener Bennett (32) and wicketkeeper Tadiwanashe Marumani (24) enjoying some batting success.
Yash Thakur claimed his first T20I wicket by dismissing Bennett. His delivery outside off was lobbed behind the stumps and Kishan made a simple catch.
Left-arm spinner Abhishek Sharma (3-17), another 2026 T20I World Cup winner, was the most successful Indian bowler.

India 219-5 in 20 overs (I. Kishan 81, T. Varma 60 not out) v Zimbabwe 129 in 17.5 overs (B. Bennett 32; A. Sharma 3-17)
Result: India won by 90 runs
Series: India have unassailable 2-0 lead before final match on Sunday

item.title: PM visits Daffodil Computers pavilion at Semiconductor Symposium and Bear Summit 2026
item.description:
Daffodil Group is showcasing Bangladesh's growing capabilities in advanced technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, smart manufacturing, and the emerging semiconductor industry at the Semiconductor Symposium and BEAR Summit 2026, held on Saturday, July 25, at the Bhashani Novotheatre in Agargaon, Dhaka.
Through an integrated technology ecosystem combining education, research, industry, and innovation, the group is demonstrating how collaboration across these sectors can accelerate Bangladesh's transition into a knowledge- and technology-driven economy.
During the summit, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited the Daffodil Computers pavilion.
He was accompanied by Fakir Mahbub Anam, MP, Minister for Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology and Ministry of Science and Technology; Rehan Asif Asad, ICT adviser to the government; and senior government secretaries.
During the visit, the Prime Minister toured Daffodil's technology exhibits, with particular focus on the laptop and ICT hardware manufacturing operations of DCL Hi-Tech.
He observed the company's manufacturing capabilities and highly appreciated the initiative, emphasizing the importance of promoting locally manufactured technology products under the "Made in Bangladesh" brand in global markets.
He also encouraged celebrating and strengthening the country's domestic manufacturing capabilities.
At one stage of the visit, the Prime Minister held a cordial discussion with Prof Md Sabur Khan, chairman of Daffodil Group.
During the discussion, Prof Khan highlighted several innovative projects and technology-driven solutions developed by students of Daffodil International University (DIU), noting that many of these innovations could be implemented to support government development initiatives in a more cost-effective and efficient manner.
The Prime Minister listened with interest and expressed his appreciation for such initiatives.
The accompanying minister and ICT adviser also endorsed the significance of the proposals.
Prof Khan also invited the Prime Minister to visit the Daffodil Hi-Tech Park, stating that the facility is playing an important role in developing Bangladesh's technology ecosystem and producing industry-ready skilled professionals.
The Prime Minister responded positively to the invitation.
During the discussion, Prof Khan further proposed reactivating the ICT Task Force, originally established in 2001 under the late former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia, to further accelerate the country's ICT sector development.
The Prime Minister assured that the proposal would receive due consideration.
Highlights of the Daffodil pavilion
DCL Hi-Tech is demonstrating its advanced electronics manufacturing capabilities, including Surface Mount Technology (SMT), Printed Circuit Board (PCB) assembly, product integration, and quality assurance processes, reflecting Bangladesh's growing capacity in electronics manufacturing.
Daffodil Robotics is showcasing innovative solutions in robotics, automation, embedded systems, and AI-powered technologies, alongside industry-oriented projects developed by students and researchers.
On the academic and research front, Daffodil International University (DIU) is presenting its initiatives in artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), cybersecurity, extended reality (XR), capstone projects, startup development, and collaborative research with industry, highlighting its efforts to develop future-ready technology professionals.
As part of its digital transformation initiatives, Daffodil Software is exhibiting AI-powered solutions including AI Professor, Central AI, the Integrated University Management System (IUMS), and 1 Card, demonstrating how artificial intelligence is enhancing education, institutional administration, and organizational efficiency.
Through its participation in BEAR Summit 2026, Daffodil Computers is strengthening opportunities for collaboration with policymakers, universities, research institutions, industry leaders, development partners, investors, and international technology organizations. The participation is also opening new avenues for research collaboration, technology transfer, joint innovation, and industry-academia partnerships.
Organizers believe that this integrated ecosystem of education, research, industry, and technology will contribute significantly to the advancement of Bangladesh's semiconductor and high-tech industries while preparing the country's young generation with the skills needed to compete in the global technology landscape.

item.title: Two Sri Lankan fishermen rescued in Maheshkhali after drifting at sea for 36 days
item.description:
Two Sri Lankan fishermen, a father and his son, who had been drifting in the Bay of Bengal for 36 days after their boat suffered an engine failure, were rescued and handed over to Maheshkhali Police on Saturday.
According to the rescued fishermen, their "Danish boat" lost engine power while they were fishing in rough weather. The boat continued drifting and eventually entered Bangladesh’s maritime territory.
They claimed that while they were stranded at sea, they were attacked by pirates, who took away all their belongings and supplies from the boat.
Local sources said fishermen from a fishing boat owned by Ziaur Rahman of South Para village under Kutubjom union in Maheshkhali spotted the stranded Danish boat carrying the two foreign fishermen in the area known as Gulirdhar while returning after fishing in the sea.
The fishermen rescued the father and son and brought the disabled boat to Tajiyakatha Ghat after tying it to their own fishing boat.
Following the rescue, the two Sri Lankan fishermen took shelter at the house of boat owner Ziaur Rahman.
Witnesses said the rescued Danish boat had no belongings inside and there were clear signs that the items kept on the boat had been looted.
Maheshkhali Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Abdus Sultan confirmed the matter, saying the two foreign fishermen are now in police custody.
He said necessary steps are being taken to verify their identities and complete the required legal and diplomatic procedures.

item.title: Two killed in bus-Nosimon collision in Munshiganj
item.description:
Two people were killed after a passenger bus collided with a Nosimon in Sreenagar upazila of Munshiganj on Saturday afternoon.
The accident occurred around 5:36pm in the Laskarpur area of the upazila.
The deceased were identified as Dulal Chandra, son of Sadhan Chandra of Khara Munipara area in Sreenagar, and Majnu Mia, son of Ayub Mia of Baraikhali area.
Majnu was driving the Nosimon, while Dulal was travelling as a passenger in the vehicle.
Deputy Assistant Director of Munshiganj Fire Service Mohammad Safiquil Islam said a Baishakhi Paribahan passenger bus, which was travelling from Baraikhali to Gulistan, collided with the Nosimon coming from the opposite direction when it reached Laskarpur.
The bus fled the scene immediately after the accident.
Local residents, police and fire service personnel rescued the injured Nosimon driver and passenger and took them to Sreenagar Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared both dead.
Police are trying to seize the bus involved in the accident. The wrecked Nosimon has been taken into police custody.

item.description:
The Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA) Trustee Board on Saturday distributed Tk1.01 crore in financial assistance among the families of those killed and injured in road accidents in Lakshmipur.
Water Resources Minister Shahid Uddin Chowdhury Anee handed over the cheques to the beneficiaries as the chief guest at a ceremony held at the Lakshmipur Sadar Upazila Parishad auditorium on Saturday.
Under the BRTA Trustee Board's assistance programme, the families of 18 deceased road accident victims received Tk5 lakh each, while 11 injured victims were given Tk1 lakh each, bringing the total disbursement to Tk1.01 crore for 29 beneficiaries.
The event was chaired by Lakshmipur Sadar Upazila Nirbahi Officer Kathoshai Pru Marma. Chandraganj Upazila Nirbahi Officer Nilufa Yasmin Nipa and BRTA Lakshmipur Executive Director Abdullah Al Mamun attended as special guests.
Addressing the programme, speakers said the financial assistance was aimed at easing the hardship faced by families affected by road accidents. They also urged the public to comply with road safety laws, follow traffic regulations and raise awareness to help prevent road crashes.
The families of the deceased and the injured beneficiaries expressed gratitude to the government for the support.
Government officials, local public representatives, journalists and members of the affected families were also present at the event.

How to start filing income tax return online
item.description:
The income tax return filing season has begun. As in the previous year, all taxpayers must submit their returns online this year.

Except for a few specific exemptions, taxpayers can no longer file returns by visiting tax offices. As a result, the online filing system has become the only available option.

Bangladesh currently has more than 12.5 million (1.25 crore) Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) holders. During the previous filing season, more than 4.5 million (45 lakh) TIN holders submitted their tax returns online.

First-time tax return filers to pay Tk 1,000 minimum tax

How to get started

You must file your income tax return online this year. Before you can do so, you need to register with the National Board of Revenue (NBR) e-Return System. To complete the registration, you will need:

  1. Your National Identity Card (NID).

  2. An active mobile phone number linked to your National Identity Card (NID).

  3. A valid Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN).

First, visit www.etaxnbr.gov.bd. Then click the 'I am not registered yet' button. Enter your TIN and mobile phone number in the required fields. You will receive a One-Time Password (OTP) on your mobile phone. Use the OTP to verify your identity and create your account password.

Online tax return filing to remain mandatory for all taxpayers in new fiscal

How to log in

Once you complete your registration, you will have access to the NBR's online tax return system and can log in whenever required.

On the day you intend to file your return, log in to the system and complete the required sections step by step by providing details of your annual income, investments, expenditure, assets, liabilities and other relevant information before submitting your return.

To log in, you will need your TIN and password. If you forget your password, you can create a new one by selecting the 'Forgot password' option.

How to pay your tax

Through the e-Return system, taxpayers can pay their income tax from home using bank transfer, debit card, credit card, bKash, Rocket, Nagad or any other mobile financial service.

Tax return mandatory for savings certificate refunds, land mutation

After providing accurate information and preparing the tax return correctly, taxpayers can submit their returns online and immediately download the acknowledgement receipt and Income Tax Certificate.

Tax incentive

From the 2026–2027 tax year, individual taxpayers who submit their income tax returns between July and September will receive an incentive equal to 5 per cent of the tax payable, subject to a maximum of Tk 25,000.

This incentive will not apply to returns submitted after September. Taxpayers who file their returns after December will be required to pay additional tax.

item.title: Gas shortage unlikely to ease right away
item.description:
The supply from liquefied natural gas (LNG) has fallen further, meaning the ongoing gas shortage is unlikely to end right away. The crisis may continue for several more days.

Authorities familiar with the matter said the floating LNG regasification terminal that converts imported LNG into pipeline gas remained out of operation on Saturday.

Gas shortages have affected several areas of the capital, including Kalabagan, Mohammadpur, Kafrul, Kazipara, West Tejturi Bazar and Badda. In some places, gas pressure is extremely low, while in others household cookers do not ignite at all.

Gas crisis deepens, disrupting cooking, transport and industry

Bangladesh operates two floating LNG regasification terminals at Maheshkhali in Cox’s Bazar to convert imported LNG into pipeline gas.

US-based company Excelerate Energy operates one terminal, while private company Summit operates the other.

A fire broke out at the Excelerate Energy terminal on Tuesday, forcing it to suspend gas supply and significantly worsening the country's gas shortage.

Bangladesh's gas sector has operated with a persistent gap between demand and supply for the past one and a half decades. Domestic gas production has also declined steadily over the past several years, increasing the country's reliance on LNG imports.

According to sources at the Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corporation (Petrobangla), the Excelerate terminal has two boilers. One boiler sustained damage in the fire.

If engineers can restart the undamaged boiler, they will be able to increase gas supply by another 300 million (30 crore) cubic feet per day. A team of specialists from the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates has been working at the terminal since Thursday.

Factories lie idle amid gas shortage, yet loan interest payments continue

Bangladesh's gas sector has operated with a persistent gap between demand and supply for the past one and a half decades.

Domestic gas production has also declined steadily over the past several years, increasing the country's reliance on LNG imports. At present, LNG accounts for between 35 and 40 per cent of the total daily gas supply.

Petrobangla Director (Operations and Mines) Md Rafiqul Islam The technical team is continuing its work, but we have not yet been able to bring the terminal back into operation. It may take more time. However, we cannot specify exactly how long it will take.

Petrobangla Director (Operations and Mines) Md Rafiqul Islam told Prothom Alo, "The technical team is continuing its work, but we have not yet been able to bring the terminal back into operation. It may take more time. However, we cannot specify exactly how long it will take."

The power sector consumes the largest share of the country's gas supply. Gas-fired electricity generation has fallen by around 1,500 megawatts, raising concerns over a power shortfall. Industry is the second-largest gas consumer.

Besides electricity generation and industrial use, gas is also used for cooking and as fuel for compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles. However, many households have been unable to use their gas cookers for several days.

Some consumers have started purchasing electric cookers, while low-income families are trying to cook with firewood using traditional clay stoves. Long queues of vehicles have also formed at CNG filling stations.

Bay of Bengal offshore gas exploration tender revised to attract bidders

Petrobangla estimates daily gas demand at 3.8 billion (380 crore) cubic feet. However, average daily supply has remained around 2.7 billion (270 crore) cubic feet since last year.

Following the fire that shut down one LNG terminal, daily gas supply has fallen to below 2.15 billion (215 crore) cubic feet.

Petrobangla issued a statement yesterday, Saturday, apologising to customers for the disruption.

The statement said domestic and international technical teams are working tirelessly to repair the technical fault at the Excelerate Energy terminal and restore operations.

Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution PLC, which supplies gas across Dhaka and neighbouring districts, said all categories of customers within its service area would continue to experience low gas pressure until the situation improves.

Customers in Mohammadpur staged a human chain protest on Friday. Consumers have also been expressing their frustration regularly in the Facebook group 'Amra Mohammadpurbashi'.

Energy expert M Tamim told Prothom Alo, "The gas sector has been hanging by a thread for a long time. The closure of one terminal has exposed the vulnerability on a large scale. Experts have been calling for alternative arrangements for years. If another onshore terminal had been in place, the current crisis might have been avoided."

item.title: Government not rushing to pick next president, whose name being discussed most?
item.description:
The government and the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) are not rushing to choose the country's next president. The government plans to hold the presidential election during the next session of the Jatiya Sangsad in September.

Before that, the BNP's National Standing Committee will decide whether to nominate a party member or someone from outside the party for the presidency. Several names are currently being discussed among party leaders and activists.

According to senior government and BNP sources, one reason for delaying the election is the proposed constitutional amendments. The government is preparing to place the 18th Amendment Bill before parliament during its next session in September.

New president likely from BNP Standing Committee
Discussions within the government and the BNP's policymaking circles suggest that, if the party nominates one of its own, the name most frequently mentioned so far is Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, minister for local government, rural development and cooperatives and BNP secretary general.

Under the Constitution, assuming the presidency would also vacate his Thakurgaon-1 parliamentary seat. Considerations such as age, physical condition, and where each leader's role is most needed within the party and the government have narrowed the list of potential candidates. The name of acting president and Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad is also being discussed in some BNP circles.

The option of nominating someone from outside the party has not been ruled out entirely. The name of a former chief justice has emerged in that context.

item.title: Sahabuddin to leave Bangabhaban; Hafiz Uddin to work there, stay at Speaker’s residence
item.description:
Former president Mohammed Shahabuddin is expected to vacate Bangabhaban today, Sunday or tomorrow, Monday. Acting President and Jatiya Sangsad Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad will then begin attending office from the presidential residence.

Shahabuddin is likely to move to his residence in Gulshan. Although the acting president will maintain his office at Bangabhaban, he will continue to live at the Speaker's official residence.

According to Bangabhaban and government sources, a departing president is entitled by law to remain at Bangabhaban for one month if he wishes. However, Mohammed Shahabuddin has already begun preparations to leave. If the preparations are completed today, Sunday, he may vacate the residence the same day.

Otherwise, he is expected to leave on Monday. On Saturday evening, Shahabuddin hosted a private dinner at Bangabhaban, attended by its officials. Although a few other formalities were expected to take place, it remains uncertain whether those will be held.

On Friday afternoon, Mohammed Shahabuddin sent his signed resignation letter to Jatiya Sangsad Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad. After receiving the letter, the Speaker announced the resignation at a press conference held in the oath-taking room of the parliament complex.

He also declared that, in accordance with the Constitution, he had assumed the responsibilities of the president. Shahabuddin stepped down nearly one year and nine months before the end of his term, citing ill health as the reason for his resignation.

Mohammed Shahabuddin was sworn in as Bangladesh's 22nd president on 24 April 2023 after being elected unopposed with the nomination of the Awami League. The presidential term is five years, meaning his tenure was due to end in April 2028. However, he is leaving Bangabhaban about 21 months before the completion of his term.

Does former President Shahabuddin enjoy immunity after leaving office?

Preparations underway at Gulshan residence

Following Mohammed Shahabuddin's resignation as president, cleaning and maintenance work is underway at his private residence in Gulshan, Dhaka. The sitting area on the ground floor is being repainted, while furniture is being cleaned.

According to people involved in managing the property, the work is being carried out in anticipation of his return within the next few days. Before becoming president, Mohammed Shahabuddin lived in a fourth-floor flat on the building.

A visit to the house on Road 123 in Gulshan on Saturday morning showed preparations in progress. Several journalists were waiting outside the residence, although no members of the law enforcement agencies were seen there.

The building's manager, Kabir Hossain, told Prothom Alo, “We do not know exactly when sir will return. But we have been instructed to make sure everything is clean and tidy. We are working accordingly. Sir may return home within the next few days.”

Reasons cited for President Shahabuddin’s resignation

A visit to the property showed a sitting room next to the car parking area on the ground floor. Several sofas and a table were placed there, with the furniture covered in polythene sheets. Several tins of paint were stacked on one side of the room. The old paint on the walls had been scraped off in preparation for repainting.

Kabir Hossain said the room would be painted first, after which the sofas would be cleaned. “People will come and sit here, so the area is being prepared,” he said.

Acting president to continue living at Speaker's residence

There can be no vacancy in the office of the president. Under the Constitution, Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad assumed the responsibilities of acting president immediately after Mohammed Shahabuddin's resignation.

Until a new president is elected and sworn in within 90 days all official duties and ceremonial functions of the presidency will be carried out by Hafiz Uddin Ahmad.

Sources at the Parliament Secretariat said Hafiz Uddin Ahmad will begin working from Bangabhaban as soon as Mohammed Shahabuddin vacates the presidential residence. Both the Office of the President and the official presidential residence are located within the Bangabhaban complex.

Although Hafiz Uddin Ahmad will perform his official duties from Bangabhaban, he will continue to live at the Speaker's official residence in the parliament complex.

Foreign ambassadors accredited to Bangladesh present their credentials to the president at Bangabhaban, while visiting foreign dignitaries also hold meetings there. Various state ceremonies are held at Bangabhaban on national days.

As a result, the official activities of the president—or, in the absence of a president, the acting president—are conducted from Bangabhaban.

After assuming the responsibilities of acting president, Hafiz Uddin Ahmad is scheduled to pay tribute at the National Martyrs' Memorial in Savar at 11:00 am today, Sunday. He will then pay his respects at the graves of former president and BNP founder Ziaur Rahman and late BNP chairperson Khaleda Zia at 12:30 pm.

item.title: Padma (Ganges) barrage and 14 problems: Why a new study is necessary?
item.description:
In 2012, a comprehensive 563-page feasibility report was submitted, covering hydrology, morphology, environment, economy, social impact, and engineering design. However, the report was for the Padma of 2012, with the climate of 2012. Now, it's 2026, and the report is 14 years old. Over these 14 years, the river, climate, diplomacy, and technology have all changed. Yet, a project worth Tk 500 billion has been approved based on this outdated survey.

Problem 1: The fundamental water calculations are questionable

The report's dry season flow calculations rest on two assumptions: firstly, that the Ganges Treaty of 1996 will remain in effect, and secondly, that the flow patterns from 1997 to 2010 will continue in the future. Both assumptions have now fallen apart.

The Ganges Treaty's term will expire in December of 2026, with no indication of a new agreement. Before the Farakka Barrage, the average dry season flow at Pangsha was 2,031 cubic meters per second. Post-treaty, it dropped to 576 cubic meters, and in some years, even lower.

Without the treaty, it is likely to decrease further. Moreover, India's upstream water withdrawal is increasing every decade. The report contains no flow data from the 16 years post-2010.

Problem 2: No lessons learned from Farakka regarding silt

The report claims that if a barrage is constructed at Pangsha, the riverbed will rise only by 3.28 feet over 60 years. Farakka's real-life experience shows that the riverbed there rose by nearly 20 feet in just 52 years. Such a significant discrepancy in a similar river with similar structures implies a fundamental flaw in the modeling approach.

The Ganges carries approximately 450 million tonnes of silt annually at Pangsha. The report mentions 18 undersluices, but these sluices' total width is only one-eighth of the entire barrage length. These could quickly become blocked in a silt-rich river and, being submerged, would be difficult to clean. When to open the sluices, how much to open them, and what strategies to employ in different seasons are not covered in the report.

Viewing Padma Barrage in light of the Teesta Barrage experience

The silt-related mathematical modeling in the report was based on 2008 data. Significant changes in the Padma's channel, silt characteristics, and quantity have occurred between 2008 and 2026. Using an outdated model in this changed context ensures incorrect results.

Problem 3: The location issue has been closed

The Pangsha point was selected in 2012 based on the river morphology at the time. In 2017, the design was canceled due to design flaws and concerns about siltation, waterlogging, and bank erosion upstream. Nine years later, the same Pangsha point has been reapproved, but the technical solutions for the 2017 issues have not been made clear to the public.

The biggest issue is that Pangsha as the only option has never been validated through a multi-criteria analysis. Selecting any location without a comparative evaluation of multiple points based on hydraulic efficiency, silt load, land acquisition level, navigation, cost, and climate resilience is like betting billions of taka on assumptions. The Padma's course has changed significantly since 2012, with new shoals, eroded banks, and a shifted main channel. Without a new survey, it's uncertain if Pangsha is still the best point.

Problem 4: The concerns of downstream people are ignored

Downstream from Pangsha to Goalanda, there is another 20 to 23 kilometers of river. If water is held back at Pangsha, the flow in this section will decrease. With Farakka blocking upstream and Pangsha blocking downstream, the river in between is drying up. The report lacks any analysis of how this "double Farakka" situation will affect the Arial Khan, Kumar, and Gorai regions.

Will the Padma (Ganges) Barrage offer a solution to the problem?

Since 1988, there have been practically no natural flows in the Gorai during the dry season. This has doubled salinity in the Khulna region and increased the peak salinity at Bardia Point eightfold. The project's objective is to reduce salinity, but without understanding the impact on downstream flow, it might have the opposite effect. This risk assessment is missing from the report.

Problem 5: No modern assessment of biodiversity

The report mentions two fish passes (passages for fish migration), but provides no further details. Farakka also had a fish pass, yet upstream hilsa production decreased by 92 per cent due to Farakka. Simply stating the number of fish passes does not fulfill responsibility. There is no analysis of the design type, effectiveness for different species, or how they will be managed and monitored.

Bangladesh's hilsa production has already decreased by over 71,000 tonnes in two years. The Ganges-Padma basin is a habitat for the endangered Gangetic dolphin. Gorai is the main freshwater source for the Sundarbans.

If the barrage obstructs the river's connection with floodplains during floods, it will destroy the habitat and breeding grounds of thousands of wetland-dependent species. Increased salinity in the Sundarbans will occur if downstream flow decreases during the dry season. There is no quantitative modeling of these environmental impacts in the 2012 report. Approving the project without such assessments according to 2026 international environmental standards is questionable.

Problem 6: Climate change impact is not accounted for

The report's entire hydrological analysis is based on historical data from 1965 to 2008. The rate of Himalayan glacier melt, monsoon patterns, and dry season flow characteristics were considerably different at that time.

The latest IPCC report indicates that by 2050, maximum monsoon flows in the Ganges-Brahmaputra basin will increase by 15-20 per cent.

The 100-year flood calculations in the report haven't been checked against this new reality to see if they are understated. Although there is a brief chapter on climate change, it is not reflected in the main design. Without projections of flow till 2050 and 2100, there's no way to determine how climate-resilient the barrage will be.

Problem 7: Structural safety requires reassessment

The report states that the barrage's foundation and structural design were based on a geological survey conducted in 2012. However, the riverbed of the Padma is highly dynamic, with its soil composition changing annually due to sediment deposition and erosion.

Without a new geological survey, the safety of the foundation cannot be assured. Moreover, the report does not reassess the probable maximum flood, seismic risk, or structural reliability in line with the latest standards of the International Commission on Large Dams (ICOLD). A failure of the barrage would put the lives of millions of people downstream at risk.

Problem 8: Future navigation left unexamined

The report mentions the construction of a navigation lock. However, it provides no detailed modelling of how the barrage would affect the depth of the navigation channel, water levels, or vessel movement upstream and downstream of Pangsha.

Inland waterborne trade in southwestern Bangladesh depends heavily on this river. Without assessing the barrage's impact on navigation, it is not possible to determine the appropriate size and design of the navigation lock.

Problem 9: No operational guidelines

Once constructed, a barrage will last 50 to 100 years. How it's operated will determine whether the project is beneficial or harmful. Modes for silt management at the start of the monsoon, storage post-monsoon, environmental flow in winter, emergency in extreme drought, and overflow during excess floods need to be defined. Who will make decisions, on what basis, and how the gates will function in these five different scenarios are not described in the report. Without operational guidelines, a barrage is like having a tool without the instructions for use.

Problem 10: Economic analysis only considers benefits, not risks

The report includes calculations of agricultural, irrigation, hydropower, and navigation benefits. However, there is no account of the long-term dredging costs upstream due to siltation, flood compensation, erosion damage, and environmental cost. Comprehensive investment evaluations include both benefits and risks. An evaluation showing only benefits is not an analysis but a promotion. The project's cost was originally estimated at Tk 314.14 billion in 2012. It has now exceeded Tk 500 billion. When basic costs increase by 60 per cent, benefits must be recalculated. This hasn't been done.

Problem 11: Resettlement plan is 13 years outdated

The report contains a land acquisition and resettlement plan. But the Padma's course and the habitation near its banks have significantly changed since 2012. Land that was submerged according to the old survey now has newly formed settlements, while some settlements have been lost to river erosion. Implementing a resettlement plan based on a 13-year-old survey will inevitably lead to land disputes and social conflict.

Problem 12: Funding source remains unclear

It’s still unclear if this Tk 500 billion project will be financed internally, through foreign loans, or via public-private partnerships. A memorandum of understanding was signed with China in 2013, but it hasn't been implemented. Without finalising the funding source, it's impossible to calculate loan terms, interest rates, and long-term financial burdens.

Approving construction with uncertain funding creates financial risk even before the project starts.

Problem 13: No analysis of diplomatic risks

This is the most significant omission in the 2012 report. The report assumes water will come and agreements will stand. However, constructing the Ganges Barrage could weaken or strengthen Bangladesh's position in negotiating a new Ganges treaty with India, but there's no analysis of this. There's also no mention that ratifying the 1997 UN Watercourses Convention is essential for any water-dispute-related negotiations.

Problem 14: This is a barrage project, not a basin plan

This is perhaps the most fundamental issue, talked about the least. The 2012 report is primarily an engineering feasibility study on how to build a structure. But the Padma's problems won't be solved by building a barrage alone. The water crisis, silt crisis, salinity crisis, biodiversity crisis are all interconnected and linked to the entire Ganges-Padma basin.

Unless the entire basin's water, silt, environment, navigation, and climate adaptation are inclusively planned around the barrage, the barrage may be constructed, but the underlying problems it aims to solve will persist.

Bangladesh's Delta Plan 2100 includes basin management, but there's no connection between that plan and this project. Approval was granted without assessing whether the construction of a standalone barrage would support or complicate the broader plan.

The 2012 report might have been adequate for its time, but in each of the fourteen fundamental problems, new information, realities, and questions have emerged by 2026. Technology has also changed significantly. Starting construction worth Tk 500 billion without addressing these fourteen questions or incorporating modern technology is a massive gamble on uncertainty.

70 million people in the southwest region are waiting for water. While their wait may be long, the project should genuinely benefit them. Bangladesh cannot afford another repeat of Farakka through rush construction based on old grounds.

#Subail Bin Alam is an engineer, founding member of the Centre for Science Tech and Policy Diplomacy, and Bangladesh Research Analysis and Information Network.
